solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Striking play that’s broadcast in front of hotel (4)

annotation.definition2: that’s broadcast in front of hotel

blocks.note: a game in which players strike a ball

blocks.clueFragment: that’s broadcast in front of hotel
blocks.note: in the NATO radio alphabet, the code word just before Hotel (H)

annotation.surface: A radio report on a round being played outside a hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on the NATO phonetic alphabet, used when spelling letters over radio: Golf, Hotel, India. 'Hotel' looks like a building but is the next code word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain sense for the club-and-ball game, plus the radio-alphabet code word that sits just before Hotel.

entries.clue: Lochinvar, extremely brave, not exactly bringing a symbol of peace (5,6)

indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.not exactly: the letters are not in exactly their original order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
the outer letters of BRAVE
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: The dashing Lochinvar, a hero of Walter Scott's poem, arrives with a peace offering.
annotation.walkthrough: Lochinvar is the romantic knight of Scott's ballad, which makes 'brave' read as praise rather than a source of two letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A symbol by example: the dove returned to Noah's ark carrying an olive twig, so it stands for peace.

entries.clue: Singer possibly flying from Cranfield far earlier (9)

indicatorNotes.flying from: the answer comes flying out of the words that follow

blocks.note: starts after CRAN and ends after the first letter of 'earlier'

annotation.surface: A pop star who left Cranfield by plane some time ago.
annotation.walkthrough: Cranfield is a town with an airfield, so 'flying' fits the surface neatly. The fieldfare is a thrush, a songbird, hence 'Singer possibly'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this thrush is a songbird, and 'possibly' flags that it is only one kind of singer.

entries.clue: Tense, fully developed short story gripping queen? Make a few copies (10)

indicatorNotes.short: a short word has lost its last letter
indicatorNotes.gripping: one word holds another inside it

blocks.note: t = tense, the grammar abbreviation
RIPE minus its last letter
a lie is a story, a fib
a queen is a female cat

annotation.surface: A writer finishes a story about a queen and wants several copies made.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Queen' points at royalty, but here it is the breeder's word for a female cat. 'Short story' is not one idea: 'short' belongs to 'fully developed'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: tripling a document gives three copies, and three counts as a few.

entries.clue: One taking part in preparing soldiers to manage without a leader (7)

annotation.definition: One taking part in preparing soldiers

indicatorNotes.without a leader: the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
MASTER (to manage) minus its first letter

annotation.surface: A drill sergeant taking part in training troops who must cope without a commander.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain, soldiers are thin strips of toast for dipping into a boiled egg, so a toaster helps prepare them. The military surface is the trap.
annotation.definitionFit: A British breakfast sense: soldiers are fingers of toast for dipping in a boiled egg, and this appliance browns them.

entries.clue: Barmiest heathen let loose simultaneously (2,3,4,6)

indicatorNotes.let loose: the letters are freed to take up a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: The craziest pagans are all released at the same moment.
annotation.walkthrough: Barmy is British slang for mad. The whole fodder is two words, so the long answer is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: things said in one breath are said at the same moment.

entries.clue: Long, essentially languid, boring time before Easter holiday spent inside (7)

annotation.type: container + middle letter + charade + outer letters

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its central letter
indicatorNotes.boring: the letter bores into another word
indicatorNotes.before: one piece comes ahead of the next
indicatorNotes.spent inside: the word's inside is used up, leaving its ends

blocks.note: Lent is the season before Easter
the central letter of LANGUID, placed inside LENT
HOLIDAY with its inside removed

annotation.surface: A long, slow, dull stretch before an Easter break spent indoors.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word seems to describe the tedium of Lent, but 'Long' is the definition and 'boring' means drilling in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something drawn out in time or extent.

entries.clue: Sotto voce utterance that could be right (5)

blocks.note: sotto voce = under the breath; a stage remark to the audience
right is one of two sides, so read the answer as two words

annotation.surface: A whispered remark that might turn out to be correct.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer: 'right' is not correct but a side, as in left and right.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre term for a remark spoken low to the audience, plus a split reading in which right is one side.

entries.clue: Attempt to speak in support of evacuated Eritreans (5)

indicatorNotes.in support of: in a down answer, the supporting piece sits beneath the other
indicatorNotes.evacuated: the word is emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

blocks.note: ERITREANS emptied of its inside
to say = to speak

annotation.surface: Someone tries to speak up for Eritrean refugees who have been evacuated.
annotation.walkthrough: The humanitarian surface hides a stacking instruction: SAY supports ES by going under it in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary verb meaning to try a task; the school essay shares the root, first meaning a trial.

entries.clue: Long to trap sheep running around in woodland — it’s wild (4,6)

annotation.definitionNote: a description of the animal rather than a synonym: a wild creature of the woods

indicatorNotes.running around: the letters run the other way round

blocks.note: to pine = to long
a net is a trap
a ram is a male sheep

annotation.surface: A wish to catch a sheep that is loose in the forest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long to trap' reads as one phrase, but PINE stands alone and NET RAM is then read backwards as a unit.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: this weasel relative is a wild animal of pine forests.

entries.clue: Biden, out of office, accepts being denied interior influence (4)

indicatorNotes.out of: one word is taken out of another
indicatorNotes.being denied interior: the word loses its interior, keeping its ends

blocks.note: BIDEN with DEN (a study, an office) taken out
ACCEPTS stripped to its first and last letters

annotation.surface: The former president, now retired, still takes on some influence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of office' suggests Biden's retirement; it actually removes DEN, a room used as a study.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a slant or prejudice that sways judgement is an influence on it.

entries.clue: Despicable individual pinching stuffing from cuddly toy. Can you understand that? (6)

indicatorNotes.pinching: one word pinches another, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.stuffing from: the stuffing of a word is its inner letters

blocks.note: git is British slang for a contemptible person
the inside of TEDDY, the cuddly toy

annotation.surface: A nasty person pulls the stuffing out of a child's soft toy.
annotation.walkthrough: The cuddly toy is TEDDY, which the solver must supply. GEDDIT is a jokey spelling of 'get it?', the phrase asking whether a joke has landed.
annotation.definitionFit: A slangy spelling of 'get it?', the tag added after a joke to check the listener followed.

entries.clue: Completely depend on unit attached to hospital department (8)

indicatorNotes.attached to: the pieces join end to end

blocks.note: ENT = ear, nose and throat department
I is the Roman numeral for one, a unit
to rely on = to depend on

annotation.surface: A patient must lean wholly on a ward in a hospital.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces appear back to front in the clue: the hospital department comes first in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adverb synonym: wholly, fully, in every part.

entries.clue: One notices fiction editor elect all over the place (3,8)

indicatorNotes.all over the place: the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A newly chosen fiction editor who is disorganised.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fiction editor' reads as one job title, but 'fiction' belongs to the definition: a machine that spots lies.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the polygraph machine picks up fiction in the sense of untruths.

entries.clue: Hood’s moll exposed in song (4)

indicatorNotes.exposed: the word is stripped of its outer letters

blocks.note: Maid Marian, Robin Hood's sweetheart
remove the outer letters

annotation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend is unmasked in a song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hood' and 'moll' conjure a gangster and his girl; the hood is Robin Hood and his sweetheart Maid Marian.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain sense: an operatic solo is a song.

entries.clue: Might this help needy mayor in a pickle? (5,5)

annotation.definition: Might this help needy mayor in a pickle?

indicatorNotes.in a pickle: the letters are in a mess

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A cash-strapped mayor in trouble wonders what would help.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a mayor short of funds in a fix would welcome cash in hand.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: cash on hand is exactly what would help a hard-up mayor in trouble, and the wordplay says the same.

entries.clue: Old-fashioned anaesthetist to prevail (9)

blocks.note: out of fashion = out
one who numbs: a numb-er

annotation.surface: An old-school anaesthetist who manages to win through.
annotation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as 'numb-er', a person who numbs, not the counting word.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: having more people on your side is one way to win out.

entries.clue: Contrive to secure best times in prime locations for profitable venture? (10)

indicatorNotes.to secure: one word secures another inside it
indicatorNotes.in prime locations: take the letters at prime-numbered positions: 2, 3, 5, 7

blocks.note: to invent = to contrive
letters 2, 3, 5 and 7 of BESTTIMES, placed inside INV…ENT

annotation.surface: Advice to time your moves well and pick prime sites for a money-making project.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prime locations' sounds like property jargon but means prime-numbered letter positions. The question mark admits not every investment profits.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, with the question mark admitting that putting money into a venture does not always pay.

entries.clue: Most considerable movements must involve one over time (7)

indicatorNotes.must involve: one word takes another into itself
indicatorNotes.over: in a down answer, a piece above another

blocks.note: tides are movements of the sea
I = one, the Roman numeral, placed inside TIDES
t = time

annotation.surface: The largest troop movements must include a single unit over a period.
annotation.walkthrough: Tidy here is the 'tidy sum' sense, meaning large, so tidiest means biggest rather than neatest.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial sense: a tidy sum is a large one, so the superlative is the biggest.

entries.clue: Where WAGs made trouble crowding nurse (4,3)

blocks.note: to tend = to nurse
to ail = to trouble, placed inside T…END

annotation.surface: Footballers' wives and girlfriends caused a fuss, mobbing a nurse.
annotation.walkthrough: WAGs are the wives and girlfriends of famous footballers in British tabloids; here the word is just wags, which a dog makes at its rear.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a dog's wags happen at its rear end.

entries.clue: On the way back, run into rain (4)

blocks.note: to run into someone = to meet them

annotation.surface: Getting caught in a downpour on the way home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run into' looks like the link to 'rain', but it is the wordplay: MEET, read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with emphasis: rain that pours down heavily.

entries.clue: Take responsibility for joint (8)

blocks.note: to take on a burden, as if on your back
the joint where arm meets torso

annotation.surface: Owning up to a share in a spliff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a shared thing or a cannabis cigarette; it is the body's joint.
annotation.definitionFit: Two plain senses: bearing a burden on your back, and the ball-and-socket joint of the arm.

entries.clue: River beneath south pole (5)

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down answer, one piece sits below the other

blocks.note: s = south
the Taff is a river in Wales, through Cardiff

annotation.surface: A river flowing below the South Pole.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South pole' reads as the Antarctic, but 'pole' is the definition and 'south' only gives S.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stout stick or rod, like a shepherd's, is a pole.

entries.clue: Special carbon cutting blade wins award (5)

indicatorNotes.cutting: the letters cut into another word

blocks.note: an oar's flat end is its blade; blade stands for oar
s = special
C is the symbol for carbon, and SC goes inside O…AR

annotation.surface: A special carbon-steel blade takes a prize.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a knife; the blade is a rowing oar.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the nickname of the Academy Award statuette for film.

entries.clue: Seasoned judge put out by damages being reduced and ultimately dismissed (6)

indicatorNotes.put out by: one letter is put out of the word
indicatorNotes.being reduced: the word is cut short at the end
indicatorNotes.ultimately: the last letter of a word

blocks.note: INJURES cut short
last letter of DISMISSED
j = judge, the letter put out of the assembled word

annotation.surface: An experienced judge sacked after a damages award is cut on appeal.
annotation.walkthrough: The legal surface makes 'damages' a payout; here it is the verb injures.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone hardened by long exposure is seasoned.

entries.clue: Cunning way to demonstrate when denied opening (4)

indicatorNotes.when denied opening: the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a march is a way of demonstrating; lose the M

annotation.surface: A crafty protest that fails to get started.
annotation.walkthrough: Arch means knowingly sly, as in an arch smile.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: knowingly sly, as in an arch look.

entries.clue: Old flame tree with merest traces of blight around trunk expected to worsen (10)

indicatorNotes.merest traces of: only the smallest part of each word, its first letter

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
acer is the maple genus
first letters of Blight Around Trunk Expected

annotation.surface: A tree with a little blight near its trunk is likely to get worse.
annotation.walkthrough: The tree-disease surface blends every piece: 'around trunk' looks like a position, but those words only supply initials.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to aggravate a bad situation, making it worse.

entries.clue: Unnatural effect, hard to work out (3-7)

indicatorNotes.to work out: the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A special effect that looks fake and is difficult to fathom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hard to work out' reads as one phrase meaning puzzling; 'hard' joins the fodder and 'to work out' signals the rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: implausible and strained, as if brought from a great distance.

entries.clue: Second from back moving to the end is unusual (4)

indicatorNotes.Second: the second letter is the one picked out
indicatorNotes.moving to the end: that letter moves to the end of the word

blocks.note: the rear is the back; its second letter E moves to the end

annotation.surface: A runner in second place from the back pulling ahead would be unusual.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second from back' looks like a position, but 'back' is REAR and 'Second' is the letter in second place.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: seldom found, uncommon, like a rare bird.
